AMEND (T) AND RECOMMIT TO CIVIL SERVICE AND PENSIONS

items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the civil service law, in relation to allowing an individual
with disabilities or a disabled veteran to hold two part-time positions
equivalent to a full-time position for purposes of eligibility for recruitment
for state employment
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6482

SPONSOR: MANNION
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the civil service law, in relation to allowing an indi-
vidual with disabilities or a disabled veteran to hold two part-time
positions equivalent to a full-time position for purposes of eligibility
for recruitment for state employment

 
PURPOSE:

The purpose of this bill is to specify that positions offered by the
Department of Civil Service to persons with disabilities may be filled
on a full-time or part-time basis.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of this bill would amend section 55-b of the Civil Service Law
by specifying that positions offered by the Department of Civil Service
to persons with disabilities may be filled on a full-time or part-time
basis.

Section 2 of this bill would amend section 55-c of the Civil Service Law
by specifying that positions offered by the Department of Civil Service
to veterans with disabilities may be filled on a full-time or part-time
basis.

Section 3 of this bill would amend section 59-d of the Civil Service Law
by requiring the Department of Civil Service to include on its website
whether employment opportunities in civil service of the State for
persons with disabilities and veterans may be filled on a full-time or
part-time basis.

Section 3 of this bill provides that the effective date shall take
effect immediately.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Disabled veterans and individuals with disabilities experience much
higher unemployment rates than those without a disability. This bill
would create more employment opportunities for individuals with disabil-
ities by creating more opportunities for part-time employment in the
State.

Currently, the Civil Service Law provides for up to 1200 civil service
positions to be filled by people with physical or intellectual disabili-
ties. This bill would amend the relevant sections of the Law to allow
each position to be filled by both full or part-time workers. Positions
designated to be filled pursuant to this section could be filled on a
full-time or part-time basis. Upon such determination, such positions
shall be classified in the noncompetitive class.

The Department of Civil Service shall make publicly available on its
website all employment opportunities in the civil service of the State
and information on obtaining employment with the State, including, but
not limited to, vacancies in the competitive, noncompetitive and labor
jurisdictional classes, announcements for upcoming open competitive and
promotional examinations, test application instructions, and desig-
nations of which employment opportunities are eligible to be filled by
individuals with disabilities and veterans with disabilities, including
whether such positions may be filled on a full-time or part-time basis.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the civil service law, in relation to allowing an indi-
vidual with disabilities or a disabled veteran to hold full-time or
part-time positions for purposes of eligibility for recruitment for
state employment

 
PURPOSE:

The purpose of this bill is to specify that positions offered by the
Department of Civil Service to persons with disabilities may be filled
on a full-time or part-time basis.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of this bill would amend section 55-b of the Civil Service Law
by specifying that positions offered by the Department of Civil Service
to persons with disabilities may be filled on a full-time or part-time
basis.

Section 2 of this bill would amend section 55-c of the Civil Service Law
by specifying that positions offered by the Department of Civil Service
to veterans with disabilities may be filled on a full-time or part-time
basis.

Section 3 of this bill would amend section 59-d of the Civil Service Law
by requiring the Department of Civil Service to include on its website
whether employment opportunities in civil service of the State for
persons with disabilities and veterans may be filled on a full-time or
part-time basis.

Section 4 of this bill provides that the effective date shall take
effect on the first of January next succeeding the date upon which it

JUSTIFICATION:

Disabled veterans and individuals with disabilities experience much
higher unemployment rates than those without a disability. This bill
would create more employment opportunities for individuals with disabil-
ities by creating more opportunities for part-time employment in the
State.

Currently, under the 55-B program, provides that up to 1700 civil
service positions can be filled by people with physical or intellectual
disabilities. This bill would amend the relevant sections of the Law to
allow such positions to be filled by both full or part-time workers.
Positions designated to be filled pursuant to this section could be
filled on a full-time or part-time basis. Upon such determination, such
positions shall be classified in the noncompetitive class. Additionally,
this bill would allow the 55-C program, for disabled veterans, to be
eligible for part-time employment.

The Department of Civil Service shall make publicly available on its
website all employment opportunities in the civil service of the State
and information on obtaining employment with the State, including, but
not limited to, vacancies in the competitive, noncompetitive and labor
jurisdictional classes, announcements for upcoming open competitive and
promotional examinations, test application instructions, and desig-
nations of which employment opportunities are eligible to be filled by
individuals with disabilities and veterans with disabilities, including
whether such positions may be filled on a full-time or part-time basis.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the first of January next succeeding the
date upon which it shall have become law.
